rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule enforce the UCF Handbook's maximum 23 hours per week rule, and does no single week (Monday-Sunday) in the Sep 15-27 period exceed this limit?
criterion: The schedule for Week 1 (Sep 15-21) and Week 2 (Sep 22-27) must each total no more than 23 hours of rehearsal time, per the UCF Stage Management Handbook maximum.
The rehearsal schedule must demonstrate awareness of cumulative weekly hours and show explicit tracking or totals across all scheduled rehearsal days within each week.

The schedule must make trade-offs to stay within the 23-hour cap — such as not scheduling every possible night, or shortening some sessions — since five 4-hour weeknights (20 hours) plus a 7-hour weekend day (27 hours total) would exceed the limit.

rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule restrict dance/movement/choreography work to Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday only, reflecting choreographer Samira Hassan's stated availability?
criterion: Any rehearsal day featuring dance, movement, or choreography work must fall on a Monday, Wednesday, or Saturday, matching Choreographer Samira Hassan's availability of 'Mon/Wed/Sat only.'
No dance, movement, or choreography rehearsals may be scheduled on Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, or Sunday.

rubrics.rubric: Does the budget reconciliation correctly cross-reference every Budget Summary category against the Expense Details line items, showing that all 7 active categories' 'Actual Spent' figures match their corresponding Expense Details sums exactly (e.g., Set Construction $1,245.80 = R-007 + R-008 + R-011 + R-013 + R-014)?
criterion: The reconciliation must cross-reference every Budget Summary category against its Expense Details line items and show that all 7 active categories match exactly: Rights & Royalties $2,800 (R-001), Scripts $337.50 (R-002), Rehearsal Space $650 (R-004 + R-006 + R-015), Set Construction $1,245.80 (R-007 + R-008 + R-011 + R-013 + R-014), Props $125.40 (R-009 + R-012), Marketing $275 (R-005 + R-010), Insurance $450 (R-003).
The reconciliation must include all 13 budget categories, including the 6 categories with $0 spent (Performance Venue, Costumes, Lighting, Sound, Orchestra, Miscellaneous).
Each category must show Budgeted, Committed/Actual Spent, Uncommitted Balance, and a Variance Flag column.

rubrics.rubric: Does the cash flow forecast correctly identify that a cash-flow gap exists in the weeks before ticket sales begin on October 1, given that cumulative expenditures ($5,883.70 already spent, plus ongoing commitments) will exceed cumulative revenue received ($2,625 to date)?
criterion: The forecast must identify that total actual revenue received to date is only $2,625 (Season Sponsor $2,000 + Program Ad Sales $450 + Donations $175) while total actual expenditures are already $5,883.70, creating a current cash-flow gap of at least $3,258.70.

The forecast must recognize that ticket sales ($20,000 projected) don't begin until Oct 1 and performances start Oct 16, meaning cumulative expenditures will significantly exceed cumulative revenue through September as spending on costumes, venue, and other items continues.
The forecast must present week-by-week figures and flag the specific weeks where cumulative spending exceeds cumulative revenue, noting the Board must cover the shortfall.

rubrics.rubric: Does the reimbursement action items list correctly identify all pending/outstanding reimbursements: Marco Vitale's four set construction purchases (R-007: $487.30, R-008: $198.50, R-011: $134.20, R-013: $312.80 all 'Pending reimbursement'), Ace Hardware R-014 ($113.00 'Not submitted'), Chris O'Brien's prop purchases (R-009: $67.40 'Pending reimbursement', R-012: $58.00 'Submitted'), and the rehearsal space charge R-006 ($250 'Pending')?
criterion: The reimbursement list must identify all 8 items requiring action: R-006 ($250, 'Pending'), R-007 ($487.30, 'Pending reimbursement'), R-008 ($198.50, 'Pending reimbursement'), R-009 ($67.40, 'Pending reimbursement'), R-011 ($134.20, 'Pending reimbursement'), R-012 ($58.00, 'Submitted'), R-013 ($312.80, 'Pending reimbursement'), and R-014 ($113.00, 'Not submitted').

Items over $200 or older than 10 days from Sep 15 must be flagged as High priority: R-006 ($250, 14 days old — High by both amount and age), R-007 ($487.30, 12 days old — High by both amount and age), R-013 ($312.80, 2 days old — High by amount). R-008 ($198.50, exactly 10 days old) is NOT High because it is not older than 10 days and is under $200.
The total outstanding reimbursement amount must be correctly calculated as $1,621.20.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Board memo provide a data-supported recommendation on whether to release the second-half budget tranche, referencing the budget utilization rate (approximately 30.1% spent: $5,883.70 of $19,525) and the current financial position?
criterion: The memo must state the current budget utilization: $5,883.70 spent of $19,525 total budget (approximately 30.1%), with $13,641.30 remaining.

The memo must analyze the financial position including: spending rate vs. timeline, upcoming major uncommitted expenses (costumes $2,500, performance venue $2,100, lighting $800, sound $1,200, orchestra $1,800), and the cash flow gap with only $2,625 revenue received against $24,400 projected.
The memo must reference the approximately $1,621.20 in outstanding reimbursements as part of the financial picture.
The memo must provide a clearly stated recommendation on whether to release the second-half budget tranche, justified by the reconciliation data and financial analysis.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Board memo include a prioritized action-item table with columns for Item, Owner, Deadline, and Status, covering at minimum: Zoe Chen's parental waiver, script distribution for outstanding copies, venue resolution for Sep 20, and outstanding reimbursements?
criterion: The memo must include a prioritized action-item table with columns for Item, Owner, Deadline, and Status (or equivalent professional format).

The table must include at minimum: (1) Zoe Chen's unsigned parental waiver (high priority, assigned to Stage Manager or Producer), (2) outstanding script copies for Zoe Chen and Hannah Blake (follow up on backorder), (3) Sep 20 venue resolution for the Youth Soccer Banquet conflict, and (4) processing the approximately $1,621.20 in outstanding reimbursements (especially those over $200 or older than 10 days).

The table must also flag the Production Team emergency contact gap — the Production Team roster lacks Emergency Contact and Emergency Phone columns, meaning 10 team members have no emergency contacts on file.

rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule ensure that each weekend in the Sep 15-27 window provides one complete day off (either Saturday or Sunday), as required by the UCF Handbook's mandatory 24-hour rest period?
criterion: For the weekend of Sep 20-21, the schedule must ensure one full day is kept completely free of rehearsal — if Saturday Sep 20 is used, Sunday Sep 21 must be off, and vice versa.
For the weekend of Sep 27-28, the schedule must similarly ensure one full weekend day is kept clear of rehearsal.

This is a non-negotiable UCF Handbook rule ('cast must have one complete 24 hour period off on a weekend — either Saturday or Sunday'), and the schedule must explicitly demonstrate compliance for each weekend in the two-week period.

rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule correctly enforce the weekend rehearsal rule of maximum 7 hours of work out of 8 hours, with a mandatory 1-hour meal break after no more than 5 hours of continuous work?
criterion: For Saturday rehearsals within the schedule (e.g., Sep 20 at Studio B 10 AM - 4 PM, or Sep 27 at Main Hall 10 AM - 6 PM), no more than 7 hours of actual rehearsal may be scheduled within any 8-hour window.
A mandatory 1-hour meal break must be included no later than 5 hours into the work day (e.g., a 10 AM start requires a meal break by 3 PM at the latest).
The schedule must explicitly show the meal break timing to demonstrate compliance with the UCF Handbook weekend rehearsal rules.
